stem:
Omar looks at the diagram of $\triangle DEF$. Two interior angles are marked $62^{\circ}$ at $E$ and $49^{\circ}$ at $F$.

Which claim correctly finds the remaining interior angle at $D$?

options.text: Angle $D$ is $62^{\circ}$, the parallel-line measure for this triangle.
Angle $D$ is $180^{\circ}-62^{\circ}=118^{\circ}$, using only one known interior angle of $\triangle DEF$.

teacher.key_rationale: Interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°, so D = 180° − (62° + 49°) = 69°. Calling D a parallel-line measure swaps the term. Adding the known angles omits subtracting from 180°. Using only one known angle leaves the triangle-sum hinge for an exterior-style supplement.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as triangle DEF with interior angles 62° at E, 49° at F, and unknown at D.
